title: DPM-Solver: A Fast ODE Solver for Diffusion Probabilistic Model Sampling in Around 10 Steps

nodes.text: DPM-Solver is a fast dedicated high-order solver for diffusion ODEs, derived from an exact formulation of the diffusion ODE solution, applicable training-free to both discrete-time and continuous-time DPMs.
nodes.evidence: we propose DPM-Solver, a fast dedicated high-order solver for diffusion ODEs with the convergence order guarantee. DPM-Solver is suitable for both discrete-time and continuous-time DPMs without any further training

nodes.text: Diffusion ODEs have a semi-linear structure (a linear function of the data variable plus a nonlinear neural-network term); prior training-free samplers ignored this structure by using black-box DE solvers, incurring discretization error on both terms.
nodes.evidence: Such structure is omitted in previous training-free samplers [3, 20], which directly use black-box DE solvers

nodes.text: An exact solution of diffusion ODEs is derived by analytically computing the linear part via variation-of-constants and, through a change-of-variable to half the log-SNR (lambda), simplifying the nonlinear part to an exponentially weighted integral of the noise-prediction network.
nodes.evidence: the solution can be equivalently simplified to an exponentially weighted integral of the neural network

nodes.text: The exponentially weighted integral formulation of the diffusion ODE solution had not been revealed in prior work on diffusion models, and connects sampling to the well-studied numerical methods for exponential integrators.
nodes.evidence: To the best of our knowledge, such formulation has not been revealed in prior work of diffusion models

nodes.text: High-order solvers (DPM-Solver-1, -2, -3) are constructed by Taylor-expanding the noise-prediction network in lambda and approximating its total derivatives using stiff order conditions, yielding solvers with convergence order guarantees.
nodes.evidence: we propose first-order, second-order and third-order versions of DPM-Solver with convergence order guarantees

nodes.text: DPM-Solver achieves 4.70 FID in 10 function evaluations and 2.87 FID in 20 function evaluations on CIFAR-10.
nodes.evidence: We achieve 4.70 FID in 10 function evaluations and 2.87 FID in 20 function evaluations on the CIFAR10 dataset

nodes.text: DPM-Solver yields a 4 to 16x speedup compared with previous state-of-the-art training-free samplers across various datasets, generating high-quality samples in only 10 to 20 function evaluations.
nodes.evidence: a 4 ∼ 16× speedup compared with previous state-of-the-art training-free samplers on various datasets

nodes.text: DPM-Solver brings training-free sampling into the 'few-step' regime (around 10 steps), whereas prior training-free samplers still required roughly 50 function evaluations for high-quality samples.
nodes.evidence: these methods still require ∼ 50 function evaluations [21] to generate high-quality samples ... we bring the efficiency of training-free samplers to a new level

nodes.text: Solving the probability flow ODE is preferred over the diffusion SDE for fast sampling because discretizing SDEs is limited by the randomness of the Wiener process, causing non-convergence at large step sizes in high dimensions.
nodes.evidence: When discretizing SDEs, the step size is limited by the randomness of the Wiener process ... A large step size (small number of steps) often causes non-convergence, especially in high dimensional spaces

nodes.text: Existing general-purpose ODE solvers (e.g. RK45 used by Song et al.) require around 60 function evaluations and fail to produce satisfactory samples in the few-step regime, motivating a customized solver.
nodes.evidence: the general black-box ODE solver used in previous work [3] empirically fails to converge in few steps

nodes.text: DPM-Solver further provides an adaptive step size schedule and supports conditional sampling with classifier guidance.
nodes.evidence: We further propose an adaptive step size schedule for DPM-Solver ... and also conditional sampling with classifier guidance
